g.text: It splits into 4 tiles: a², ab, ab, b²
Add the tiles: a² + ab + ab + b²
The two grey ab tiles are identical,
Start with the full square: a²
Remove two strips, each a × b: − ab − ab
The corner b² was removed twice,
so add it back once: + b²
The white square left over has side
(a − b), so its area is (a − b)².
Take a² and cut out the corner b²
Cut the L-shape into two rectangles
Rotate the small one and attach it
Same pieces, same area: the L-shape
Adding the two squares cancels the 2ab
pieces, leaving two a² and two b² tiles.
A cube of side (a + b) splits into 8 blocks
Same idea as the square, one dimension up:
count the blocks of each shape.
Start with the whole cube: a³
The corner block b³ must go too: − b³
The white cube left over has side (a − b),
by every term of (a² + b² − ab)
Cells with matching shades cancel to zero
Only the white cells remain: a³ + b³
Sum of cubes: a³ + b³ always
by every term of (a² + b² + ab)
Cells with matching shades cancel to zero
Only the white cells remain: a³ − b³
Difference of cubes: a³ − b³ always
Side of the big square = a + b + c
Equal pairs: ab + ab, bc + bc, ca + ca
Each tile is a product of two sides;
add all nine tiles to expand the square.
(a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)
Multiply every term of (a + b + c)
by every term of the second bracket
Cells with matching shades cancel to zero
White cells remain: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc
If a + b + c = 0 the product is zero, so
